points.t: Itch **worse at night**, itchy contacts, **burrows** in finger webs, wrists, genitals.
*Sarcoptes scabiei* burrows in the stratum corneum; itch is a **delayed hypersensitivity**.
**Permethrin 5%** whole body, repeat after 7 days, for every close contact on the same night.
**Crusted (Norwegian) scabies** in a frail or immunosuppressed person: same-day specialist.

cause.lead: A mite that tunnels and an immune reaction that itches.
points: Spread by **prolonged skin-to-skin** contact (household, sexual, carer). Handshakes rarely.
Female burrows in the stratum corneum and lays eggs; larvae hatch in 3–4 days.
**Itch starts 3–6 weeks** after first infestation (1–3 days on re-infestation): contacts spread it before they itch.
**Crusted**: thousands–millions of mites when immunity or scratching fails (frailty, dementia, immunosuppression, potent steroids).

visuals.caption: A burrow in the outermost skin layer: the female mite at the leading end, with eggs and faecal pellets behind her. The itchy papule comes from the immune reaction in the dermis below.
visuals.alt: Skin section with a scabies burrow, mite and eggs

features.lead: Burrows are the proof; look where mites like it warm.
points: Generalised itch, worse at **night** and after a warm bath; **contacts itchy** too.
**Burrows**: short wavy grey threads (2–10 mm), mite at the leading end.
Secondary eruption: excoriated papules, eczematised patches away from burrows.
**Nodules** in axillae, groin, penis / scrotum; may persist after cure.
**Infants**: palms, soles, face, scalp. **Older adults**: few signs, back involved.
**Skin of colour**: violaceous or hyperpigmented papules.

visuals.caption: Where to look: finger webs and sides of fingers, front of wrists, elbows, front armpit folds, nipples, waistband and navel, and groin. The head and neck are usually spared in healthy adults.
visuals.alt: Body map of typical scabies sites

items.name: Dermoscopy
items.t: Dark ‘delta-wing jet’ at the burrow end.

items.name: Genital papules
items.t: Itchy papules on penis or scrotum: highly suggestive.

items.name: Crusted
items.t: Thick grey-yellow crusts; itch may be mild.

points: Night itch + itchy contacts + typical sites + burrows.
Washable ink over a burrow, wipe with alcohol: ink tracks the tunnel.
‘Delta-wing jet’; microscopy for mites, eggs, scybala.
Offer an **STI screen**; GUM for partner notification.

cards.name: Atopic eczema
cards.clue: Flexural, atopy; no burrows; contacts not itchy.

cards.name: Insect bites
cards.clue: Grouped on exposed sites; pets or bed bugs.

cards.name: Dermatitis herpetiformis
cards.clue: Grouped vesicles on elbows, knees, buttocks; coeliac.

cards.name: Pompholyx
cards.clue: Deep palm vesicles; no trunk or genital papules.

cards.name: Body lice
cards.clue: Lice and eggs in clothing seams; homelessness.

manage.lead: Treat the household, not just the patient (NICE CKS / BNF).

points: Treat **everyone at once**: household, sexual partners (past month), carers.
Day 1: hot-wash and tumble bedding, towels, clothes, or bag for 3–4 days.
Children return to school **after the first treatment** (UKHSA).

rx.dose: Whole body from neck down incl. webs, under nails, genitals, soles; leave 8–12 h
rx.note: ~30 g per adult application. Include scalp, face, ears if < 2, ≥ 65, immunocompromised or lesions there. OK in pregnancy and breastfeeding. P medicine from 2 months.
Avoid in pregnancy, breastfeeding, < 15 kg. Check formulary.

points: Lasts **2–4 weeks** (nodules longer): not failure.
Crotamiton 10%, hydrocortisone 1% once mites cleared, emollients, night-time sedating antihistamine.
New burrows or itch > 2–4 weeks after last dose: check technique and contacts.

limits.t: Can mask scabies or encourage crusted disease.
Irritant dermatitis is a common cause of ‘failure’ itch.
Paraffin products on fabrics catch fire easily.

items.t: Suspected **crusted scabies**: specialist advice; isolation and outbreak control in care homes.
Failure after two correct courses with all contacts treated.
Significant secondary infection, systemic illness, or diagnostic doubt.

pearls.t: Say the itch won’t stop at once: prevents over-application.
Cut nails short; cream under nails; reapply to hands after every wash; mittens on infants.
Pregnancy: permethrin first; malathion alternative; avoid ivermectin.

quiz.q: How is permethrin 5% applied and repeated?
quiz.a: Whole body from the neck down (incl. webs, under nails, genitals, soles), left 8–12 h, repeated after 7 days.

quiz.q: Who else must be treated, and when?
quiz.a: All close contacts (household, sexual partners in the past month, carers) on the same night, symptomatic or not.

quiz.q: Why do contacts need treatment without itch?
quiz.a: Itch is a delayed hypersensitivity starting 3–6 weeks after first infestation: they can be infested and infectious already.
Usually post-scabetic itch (hypersensitivity), not failure. Review if beyond 2–4 weeks or new burrows.

quiz.q: Care-home resident with thick crusts and itchy staff?
quiz.a: Suspect crusted scabies: same-day specialist advice and outbreak control.
